decision_conditions: The proposed first floor side extension, when considered cumulatively with the scale and extent of development already carried out on the site, would result in an overdeveloped and visually dominant form of development that would fail to remain subordinate to the original dwelling. The proposal would materially erode the remaining visual gaps between the dwelling and neighbouring properties, giving rise to a cramped appearance that would undermine the spacious character and established pattern of development within the Copse Wood Estate Area of Special Local Character. By reason of its cumulative bulk, massing and siting, the development would be harmful to the character and appearance of the host dwelling, the street scene and the wider Area of Special Local Character, contrary to Policies BE1 and HE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One (2012), Policies DMHB 5, DMHB 11, DMHB 12 and DMHD 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), and Policy D4 of the London Plan (2021).

In the absence of an Arboricultural Impact Assessment, Tree Protection Plan or method statement, the proposal fails to demonstrate that the increased extent of hardstanding and the formation of a dropped kerb within the root protection area of an existing tree identified as T4 (Purple Leaf Plum - Category C1) could be carried out without causing harm to the tree or prejudicing its long-term retention. In addition, the submitted plans fail to adequately demonstrate the retention and treatment of existing boundary planting, including an established hedge that contributes positively to the landscaped character of the frontage and the Area of Special Local Character. As such, the proposal raises concern that existing trees and landscaping would not be satisfactorily protected or retained, to the detriment of urban greening, visual amenity and Area of Special Local Character. The development is therefore contrary to Policies DMHB 5, DMHB 11 and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.
description: Erection of first floor side extension, and addition of driveway and dropped kerb to front
